subject: Mathematics
misconceptionDescription: Learner assumes both numerators and denominators must be added together, resulting in e.g. 1/4 + 1/4 = 2/8.
diagnosticQuestion: If you take one slice from a 4-slice pizza and another slice from the same pizza, do you get smaller slices or more slices?
correctionStrategy: Clarify that the denominator defines the partition slice size (the unit) while the numerator counts how many slices you hold.
verificationQuestion: If a chocolate bar has 6 equal pieces, and you eat 2 pieces in the morning and 3 pieces in the evening, what fraction of the whole bar have you eaten?

subject: Mathematics
misconceptionDescription: Learner applies whole number intuition to denominators, assuming 1/8 > 1/4 because 8 > 4.
diagnosticQuestion: If you share one dosa equally among 8 friends, will each person get more or less dosa than sharing among 4 friends?
correctionStrategy: Demonstrate inverse proportion: dividing a whole into more parts makes each part smaller.
verificationQuestion: Would you rather have 1/2 of a cake or 1/10 of the same cake if you want the bigger piece?

subject: Science
misconceptionDescription: Learner assumes plants get their food and building material directly out of dirt through roots like an animal mouth.
diagnosticQuestion: When a tiny acorn grows into a huge 500-kilogram oak tree, does the soil around the roots lose 500 kilograms of dirt?
correctionStrategy: Explain that roots absorb water and dissolved minerals, but the actual carbon atoms that build the plant wood and leaves come from air (carbon dioxide) via photosynthesis.
verificationQuestion: Where does the carbon that forms the solid trunk of a giant neem tree mainly come from?

subject: Mathematics
misconceptionDescription: Learner assumes -10 > -2 because 10 is greater than 2.
diagnosticQuestion: If city A is at -10 degrees Celsius and city B is at -2 degrees Celsius, which city is colder?
correctionStrategy: Use the vertical depth or number line model: values to the left on the number line are always smaller.
verificationQuestion: Which temperature is warmer: -5 degrees or -1 degree?
